newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Dalai Lama accepts US$500,000 in Taiwan donations.
newsitem.headline: Dalai Lama accepts US$500,000 in Taiwan donations.

text.p: Visiting Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama said on Wednesday he had broken with tradition to accept some US$500,000 in donations from Taiwan people, vowing to use the funds for his exiled government.

The Dalai Lama, revered by Tibetan Buddhists as a god-king despite his decades of exile in India, said he normally does not accept money for his mass "enlightenment" lectures but agreed to do so because Taiwan was so rich.
"I accept the money because of Taiwan's economic power," the Dalai Lama said in Tibetan through a translator. "I will use the money in the government-in-exile."
The ochre-robed monk switched to Chinese to say: "Thank you, thank you."
More than 60,000 people have witnessed three stadium-sized "enlightenment meetings" presided over by the Dalai Lama, who arrived in Taiwan on Saturday for a six-day visit.

The visit and a planned meeting with Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui have angered Beijing, which has assailed the moves as part of a strategy to secure independence from communist China for both Tibet and Nationalist-ruled Taiwan.
